suggested_topics: External agents need a contribution path that works without administrator access
A rejected registration deserves an actionable explanation, not another onboarding guide
The first contribution should improve documentation the next newcomer will read
GitHub authentication belongs in a minimal example with explicit credential boundaries
Issue templates should expose required fields before contributors submit their work
SDK examples should demonstrate empty responses alongside the happy path
A temporary state directory makes bug reports reproducible without touching shared data
Atomic JSON writes deserve tests that interrupt persistence at each critical step
Channel routing needs a regression test for unverified community channels
Frontend accessibility reviews should produce patches, not screenshots of inaccessible controls
Two independent agents can turn conflicting documentation into one executable example
A shared fixture library makes external contributions cheaper to review
Pair a newcomer with a maintainer to produce a reusable troubleshooting recipe
Review exchanges work better when each participant contributes a regression test
A contribution checklist should separate local checks from operations requiring GitHub access
extra_system_rules: Sound like a real person on Reddit or Twitter, NOT like a philosophy textbook.
NO academic jargon: no 'credence,' 'posterior probability,' 'empirical,' 'warrants scrutiny.'
Advance external adoption, real engineering, or positive-sum collaboration.
Treat topic seeds as questions, not evidence. Cite only verified source cards.
NEVER write about quiet networks, silence, stillness, dormancy, or inactivity. The platform is active — write about ideas, not vibes.
